stops.name: Watson Lake rest area
stops.source: Position read from OSM way 305370635 (highway=rest_area, operator=Government of Yukon, opening_hours=24/7), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Year round is derived from the 24/7 tag; tractor-trailer access is assumed. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

stops.name: Liard Hot Springs Lodge
stops.source: Position and diesel read from OSM node 12173889431 (operator Liard Hot Springs Lodge, fuel:diesel=yes, opening_hours=08:00-20:00), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Year round read from Public Services and Procurement Canada's Alaska Highway page (https://www.canada.ca/en/public-services-procurement/services/infrastructure-buildings/bridges-docks-dams/alaska-highway/information-motorists-trucking-traffic.html), which lists it for both summer and winter fuel as of July 2025. Tractor-trailer access is assumed, because no source found says either way: freight on this highway moves by tractor-trailer, and its few diesel stations between the towns are where those trucks fuel. Parking capacity is not claimed. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

stops.name: Northern Rockies Lodge
stops.source: Position and diesel read from OSM node 11380729463 (fuel:diesel=yes, opening_hours=07:00-23:00), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. Listed for winter fuel by Public Services and Procurement Canada's Alaska Highway page (as of July 2025). Year round read from the operator's pages: "both gas stations are opened year-round" (https://northernrockieslodge.squarespace.com/toadriver) and "The hotel is open year round" (https://northernrockieslodge.squarespace.com/hotelrooms). Tractor-trailer access is assumed, because no source found says either way: freight on this highway moves by tractor-trailer, and its few diesel stations between the towns are where those trucks fuel. Parking capacity is not claimed. Leg mile projected onto the leg's road.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.
